arguments.name: Naturalistic theories fail to explain the minimal facts
arguments.conclusion: Naturalistic theories cannot adequately explain the minimal facts, and most critics have given up on them.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The minimal facts (six facts conceded by ~95% of scholars) can give the major refutation of every naturalistic theory.
P2: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories.
P3: Bart Ehrman says, 'History can't prove miracles, but neither can history disprove miracles.'
P4: More critical scholars now accept either a bodily resurrection or a real appearance experience (Casper view) rather than denying the resurrection entirely.

st5.quote: Critics will generally allow this today that Jesus predicted it ahead of time.

st7.quote: It could be a critical comeback.

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas & Antony Flew, 'Did Jesus Rise from the Dead?', 1987 (minimal-facts method)

or1.quote: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories.
or1.why: Same minimal-facts-vs-naturalistic-theories argument Habermas has run since the 1980s, updated with newer skeptic names.

or2.quote: More and more critics, they are unbelievers, but they're treating us like it's a draw.
or2.why: Adds the Casper-view / 'it's a draw' survey claim as new support.

or3.quote: History can't prove miracles, comma. But neither can history disprove miracles.
or3.why: Bridges historiography into the epistemology of miracle claims.

or4.quote: If you take this approved list, you can refute you can give the major reputations of every naturalistic theory.
or4.why: No formalization or model is added.

arguments.weakest_link: P1: no naturalistic theory is actually tested against the six facts; the refutation is asserted, not shown.
arguments.develop_next: Take the strongest surviving naturalistic theory and show premise-by-premise which minimal fact it contradicts.

arguments.name: Early testimony unique among world religions
arguments.conclusion: Christianity has earlier and better-attested historical sources than any other religion or ancient figure.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The earliest sources for Alexander the Great are about 300 years after his death.
P2: Buddhist sources are 600-800 years after Buddha.
P3: Paul Barnett, an Australian historian, says nothing in ancient history, secular or religious, has anything like the early Christian testimony.
P4: Even Bart Ehrman admits we have high Christology texts from 2-3 years after the cross.

st3.quote: In fact, um Paul Barnett, an Australian historian, says he's taught world religions.

st4.quote: The 600 800 years comprise good history. Don't work.

st6.quote: nothing in ancient history, secular or religious, has anything like this.

arguments.prior_art: Paul Barnett, 'Is the New Testament Reliable?', 1986 (and standard Christian apologetic comparisons of source-gap dates)

or1.quote: He says nothing in ancient history, secular or religious, has anything like this.
or1.why: A familiar apologetic comparison of testimony dates, here voiced through Barnett and Ehrman.

or2.quote: When you open up page one, here's what the book says to my Christian readers. We don't have what you have.
or2.why: Uses a Buddhist-edition preface as fresh comparative evidence.

arguments.weakest_link: P3: the uniqueness claim rests on one authority's assertion rather than a systematic comparison of source-to-event gaps.
arguments.develop_next: Give a table of source-to-event gaps for a fixed set of ancient figures so the comparison is checkable.
